newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sets first mass selloff tender Oct 7-25.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sets first mass selloff tender Oct 7-25.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to hold its first mass sell-off tender October 7-25, where shares of 968 state firms will be auctioned as part of the country's delayed mass privatization program.

"Bulgarians will be able to buy shares in 968 enterprises or 92 percent of all firms earmarked for mass privatization in the first tender, scheduled to be held October 7-25," Mass Privatisztion Center chief Kalin Mitrev told a news conference.

Some three million Bulgarians or around 46 percent of the eligible population have bought voucher booklets, each with a face value of 25,000 levs, which would enable them to take part in the program, launched earlier this year to speed up restructuring. They can participate directly in the auctions, through the local post stations, or through some 80-odd privatization funds approved by the Stock Exchange and Securities Commission.

The enterprises slated for mass privatisation include metal smelters, chemical fertalizer producers, a tire maker and food processing plants, among others. Firms which are not sold in the first tender will be offered in the second mass privatization tender, due in several months, said Mitrev.
